approach.method_basis: The Parent learns a recurrent SMILES language prior from an unlabeled molecular corpus, then starts each objective with a fresh policy copied from that frozen prior. After each accepted batch, it trains on the best-scoring half of the current molecules and the highest-scoring eligible historical elites. A memory retains the thirty-two strongest accepted elite identities with their original strings and scores. Every selected sequence receives equal loss weight and a target equal to its frozen-prior log probability plus sixty times its accepted score. Bounded clipped Adam steps fit those targets, and the updated policy directly samples complete molecules with chemical validation and canonical duplicate rejection. Stronger-history selection is already part of this Parent; its passive uniform replay comparison only measures that selection.
approach.novelty: Add conditional joint target normalization. Treat the unchanged selected current and historical sequences as distinct outcomes of one probability model. If their proposed probability masses sum above one, subtract the log of that sum from every selected log-likelihood target; otherwise leave every target unchanged. This removes a shared impossible probability demand while preserving all pairwise target differences, including the inherited reward and prior preference. It differs from the lineage siblings that changed prior learning, replay membership, memory retention or equivalent strings. An earlier experiment in another lineage removed common policy credit and performed worse; this experiment instead changes fixed likelihood targets only when their joint mass is impossible. A same-state comparison against the raw Parent targets will measure the resulting learning change. Better probability accounting may help subsequent search, but it does not guarantee broader chemistry or a score gain.

observed_bottleneck: Parent n-06c043e9d303 has confirmed stronger-history replay and a complete three-seed macro mean of 0.5132724550531974, but its target rule independently adds reward to every selected sequence without accounting for their shared probability mass. A read-only audit of all fifteen actual task logs, excluding each terminal update, finds 435 prospective updates and 4,275 selected row exposures. In 239 updates, logsumexp of the unchanged augmented targets exceeds zero; 1,108 row targets are individually positive, including 595 of 2,100 historical exposures. Three joint violations occur even though every individual target is nonpositive. The maximum target log mass is 41.36836089992916. These are necessary normalization violations for distinct completed sequences, not a claim that a finite recurrent model can fit every normalized target. The Parent Curate observation also records 834 historical rows whose raw target error worsens, raw duplicate draws increasing from its Parent's 30.11% to 40.78%, and an uneven paired mean gain of 0.005718402034624055. Those observations motivate testing persistent impossible likelihood pressure without asserting it caused the concentration. Historical-replay evidence in n-15499bde2e65 and n-0f987622ee3c retains the same limitation. The failed common-credit experiment n-f5cfa75eff1c warns that removing a common learning component can reduce useful transfer, making a conditional, directly audited target change essential.
hypothesis: Conditionally normalize the unchanged selected current-and-historical augmented likelihood targets by a single shared offset: for a_i = frozen_prior_log_likelihood_i + 60 * accepted_score_i, fit t_i = a_i - max(0, logsumexp_j(a_j)) over the actual selected training union, preserving equal row weights, pairwise target differences and every target when its joint probability mass is already at most one.

finding_summary.headline: Target normalization changed learning and reduced fit error; two docking replicas failed to finish
finding_summary.insights:
Removing impossible selected-target demands is sufficient to change the learner, but insufficient to preserve useful generation. Across the same 415 successful suggestion positions, the child used 73,384 raw draws versus 35,144 for the parent. Its duplicate fraction fell from 38.92% to 10.33%, while its unterminated fraction rose from 0.003% to 44.21%; the two failed requests add a further 131,112 draws. Lower duplication therefore did not mean a more productive sampler. Both updates immediately before those failures reduced projected fitting error and had measurable gradient changes, so successful normalization and fitting do not rule out loss of sequence completion. The evidence identifies a failure in the resulting proposal distribution, but does not isolate which token changes caused it.

The condition itself has strong controls: all three median-similarity sessions and two sitagliptin sessions never needed normalization and reproduced their parent molecule-and-score trajectories exactly. Every trajectory that changed first diverged after a positive-offset update. In the useful history-bearing opportunities, the common shift reversed 722 selected rows from upward likelihood pressure to downward pressure, even though their relative target preferences were preserved. This narrows the unresolved question to what the shifted regression does to shared sequence-model support, including termination and molecules outside the fitted union. The supplied chemistry assessment finds recognizable compact aromatic and basic-amine families among the leaders alongside attachment drift, excessive chain or ring growth, and absent stereochemical specification. A necessary probability bound on selected strings does not resolve those chemical limitations. The completed-task gains justify studying the conditional target effect further only with generation reliability and useful chemical transfer measured alongside fitting.
finding_summary.results:
The intended target and learning changes occurred. Of 430 recorded updates, 232 needed normalization. All 232 removed excess joint target probability mass, eliminated all 1,252 individually positive log-probability targets, preserved the differences between selected targets within the registered tolerance, and changed the combined learning gradient. The other 198 updates retained their targets exactly and had identical projected-target and raw-target gradients. Among the 219 history-bearing positive-offset updates followed by a successful proposal batch, pooled projected mean squared error fell from 164.659 to 9.544 and decreased in every update. Current-example error fell from 311.898 to 13.978 and historical-example error from 17.421 to 5.110. Individual historical errors still worsened in 288 of 1,095 exposures. The raw-target error, measured at those same before/after policy states, rose from 263.347 to 286.769; the optimizer was fitting the changed objective.

Search reliability deteriorated despite those fitting gains. Thirteen of fifteen task replicas completed their 300 evaluations. Docking seeds 0 and 2 stopped at 260 and 140 evaluations because the policy could not refill a valid novel batch. In their final failed requests, 60,076 of 65,544 draws and 65,553 of 65,568 draws did not terminate. The child therefore has no complete three-seed macro mean. The sole complete seed scored 0.527720 versus its parent’s 0.514385, a paired gain of 0.013335. Among tasks completed in all three seeds, mean final-best score increased from 0.459183 to 0.471568 for zaleplon and from 0.601097 to 0.718554 for scaffold hopping, stayed at 0.218884 for median similarity, and fell from 0.288538 to 0.286001 for sitagliptin. These completed-task results cannot establish the proposed three-seed macro improvement.

molecular.headline: Aromatic medicinal scaffolds and basic cyclic amines are present; attachment drift, oversized tails and unspecified stereochemistry remain.
molecular.overall_character: The output contains recognizable hydroxybenzamides, fused nitrogen heterocycles, anilinoquinazolines, arylsulfonyl piperazines, tricyclic arylamines and acylhydrazones. Ring chemistry is abundant: the taskwise ring_closure_rate ranges from 0.9716 to 0.9977, and aromatic_atom_rate from 0.906 to 0.9954. These are fractions of proposed SMILES containing the corresponding textual features, not perceived ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions. Mean SMILES lengths range from 38.8 to 45.5; they are string lengths, not molecular weights. Ordinary medicinal-sized structures coexist with much larger polyaryl, oligomeric and polymethylene outliers. The strongest families often look synthetically plausible by inspection, but unusual connectivity and extreme ring or chain growth make the complete output questionable as a ready-to-make collection. Structural diversity is moderate across trajectories and seeds, with much narrower high-score families. Every task has stereocentre_rate 0.0: potential stereocentres exist, but tetrahedral configuration is not encoded. All requested tasks have trajectories. The docking record is partial in two seeds, so its final excerpt must not be read as the endpoint of three completed runs. These are chemical readings of supplied structures and scores, not measured synthesis, stability, pharmacology or mechanism activation.

per_task.generated_character: The highest-scoring molecules are compact aromatic amides: phenolic benzamides bearing pyridylmethyl groups on the amide nitrogen, and hydroxy dimethylquinoline carboxamides bearing benzyl substituents. They combine aromatic or fused heteroaromatic rings with carbonyl acceptors, phenolic donors and ring nitrogens; some close analogues add halogen or nitrile substitution. These are recognizable, apparently makeable medicinal scaffolds. The amide nitrogen itself is not an ordinary basic amine. The low-score tail instead includes much larger polyaryl, repeatedly amidated structures and heavily substituted flexible assemblies. Compared with parent n-06c043e9d303, whose high scorers included azaindole ester amides, pyrazole carboxamides and heteroarylmethyl ureas, the child emphasizes different compact amide families; neither output lacks rings.
liabilities: Repeated aryl-amide growth produces very large, flexible, highly substituted structures with poor visible scores and a much less convincing medicinal size envelope.

The bis(pyridylmethyl) amides retain flexible benzylic links, while late catechol-like and N-hydroxy variants introduce additional chemical liabilities without reliable score improvement; stability was not measured.
missing_features: Many weak and final proposals fail to preserve the compact amide plus appropriately positioned aromatic nitrogen and hydroxyl arrangement seen in the better families.

Controlled alternative linkages that retain that donor/acceptor arrangement while changing flexibility are not demonstrated among the cited leaders. Any benefit from an unobserved scaffold remains unknown.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The phenolic bis(pyridylmethyl) benzamide reaches 0.48839749189747395, whereas the cited long polyaryl polyamide scores 8.44294806417311e-77. Within the benzamide family, a para-hydroxy analogue scores 0.46499055497527714, while replacing the hydroxyphenyl acyl group with a small oxygen/nitrogen heteroaryl group gives 0.13118230142245307. A final N-hydroxy amide that also loses a pyridylmethyl substituent scores 0.0053395148832984345; those simultaneous changes cannot be assigned separate effects. The initial trimethoxy indole carboxamide already scores 0.3051048083696145. The visible gradient therefore favors compact, specifically connected aromatic amide/heteroatom combinations, and sharply rejects excessive elaboration; it does not establish a missing reference pharmacophore.

per_task.generated_character: The leading family consists of relatively compact, predominantly planar anilinoquinazolines: a fused nitrogen heteroaromatic core linked through NH to a fluorinated phenyl ring. The best examples add a phenol, with either fluorine or an amidine elsewhere on the fused core. Other high examples carry nitro, halogen, ester, or methoxy-substituted alkynyl side chains. This is an intelligible medicinal series with plausible conventional members, rather than a shortage of aromatic complexity. The halogen_rate is 0.8356 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.9954. Parent high scorers instead included fluorinated hydrazone, aminomethyl aryl and imine/thiourea assemblies; the child high-score family changes the core connections as well as its decorations.
liabilities: Dense aromatic and halogen substitution concentrates the leading series in a narrow chemical family; solubility and other physical properties have not been measured.

Nitro substituents, an unusual charge-separated sulfur group and a strained ring-contracted final structure merit chemical scrutiny. Their accepted scores do not establish stability or synthetic accessibility.
The methoxy-substituted alkynyl side-chain examples contain potentially stereogenic carbon without encoded configuration.
missing_features: Most weaker members lack the phenolic decoration in the same retained anilinoquinazoline context; functional-group identity and attachment location are not consistently maintained.

Broader high-scoring scaffold alternatives with comparably organized donors and ring-nitrogen acceptors are not demonstrated. The record does not show that added saturation or a basic aliphatic amine would improve this objective.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The phenolic anilinoquinazoline scores 0.8885781306387586 and its phenol/amidine relative 0.8845962113659023. Retaining the anilinoquinazoline but using the cited nitro decoration gives 0.6807958477508651, and the fluorine/chlorine analogue gives 0.6652249134948097. The low-score sulfone-containing fused heterocycle gives 0.2852486355366889. A tiny initial alkyl bromide already scores 0.5, so a value near that level is not evidence of useful chemical similarity by itself. The contrast supports the specific heteroaromatic/anilino arrangement and phenolic decoration more strongly than simply increasing fluorination or ring count. The amidine is optional in the best examples, not an established requirement.

per_task.generated_character: The supplied trajectories contain 260, 300 and 140 evaluations in seeds 0, 1 and 2 respectively, totaling the digest's 700 molecules. The highest-scoring excerpt is dominated by seed 1: N-alkyl or N-alkynyl piperazines and expanded diazacycles attached to a tricyclic diarylamine framework with saturated carbon bridges. They carry a credible protonatable aliphatic nitrogen beside substantial hydrophobic ring surfaces; basic cyclic amines are clearly present. Other seeds show tricyclic piperidine and flexible diamine families. Parent trajectories also contain high-scoring basic cyclic amines and flexible diamines, although their aromatic frameworks differ. Many of these ordinary-sized amine scaffolds are apparently makeable. At the opposite extreme, the final seed-2 excerpt includes immense polymethylene cyclic amidine and lactam structures that are chemically remote from the leading ligands.
liabilities: Extreme polymethylene ring growth, reaching the digest's maximum SMILES length of 154, creates obvious size and conformational liabilities; a ring-closure digit alone does not imply useful ring chemistry.
Long alkyl or alkynyl tails and expanded diazacycles add flexibility and hydrophobic burden to otherwise recognizable scaffolds. Those properties and biological selectivity were not measured.
The final excerpt belongs to the shortened seed-2 trajectory and must not be presented as the final chemical state of every seed.
missing_features: Many weak proposals lack the successful combination of an accessible basic aliphatic nitrogen, bounded linker length and organized aromatic surface, even when they contain numerous nitrogen atoms.

The record does not demonstrate stereochemically specified alternatives around the successful amine/ring arrangements. It provides no evidence that a particular unobserved stereoisomer would score better.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The alkynyl piperazine/tricyclic diarylamine reaches 0.9999940500545967; its shorter bridged analogue scores 0.9999908104453891 and an N-butyl analogue 0.9999903297149165. The cited nitro heteroaryl acid scores 1.8588450134335675e-05, and the sulfonamide containing a sulfonylated piperidine scores 1.9828327575562915e-05. This contrast is consistent with a properly presented protonatable amine and hydrophobic framework being useful; amide or sulfonamide nitrogen is not an equivalent substitute. The huge final cyclic amidine and lactam both receive 0.02885837683273086, which does not make their structures credible leads. The digest median is 0.007175, so the excellent leading family is not representative of most evaluated structures. These observations do not establish binding poses or why the shorter trajectories stopped.

per_task.generated_character: The better molecules are arylsulfonyl piperazines joined to fused heteroaromatic lactam or cyclic ether/ketone frameworks, together with biaryl and alkoxy analogues bearing N-methylpiperazine. They have substantial aromatic surfaces, saturated diazacycles, sulfonyl acceptors and, in the leading fused series, a carbonyl and additional nitrogen functionality. These are recognizable, mostly plausible medicinal structures of moderate to relatively large size. The sulfonylated nitrogen is not basic; some N-methylpiperazine examples retain another protonatable nitrogen. The wider set also includes carbamates, imides, hydrazones and sulfur-rich heterocycles, as well as tiny fragments. Molecular identities and scores match parent n-06c043e9d303 in evaluation order across every supplied seed; the chemistry has not changed in these trajectories.
liabilities: Tiny reactive or unusual fragments, including an organic azide and N-hydroxy trichloromethyl formamide, coexist with the plausible medicinal families.
Some larger sulfur-rich and hydrazone-containing proposals have complicated connectivity or unspecified imine geometry without a clear benefit in the supplied scores.
missing_features: The weak tail lacks the integrated arylsulfonyl/cyclic-diazamine arrangement, and often the fused carbonyl-bearing ring, that co-occur in the leading examples.

Consistent exploration of alternative attachments while retaining that complete polar/aromatic combination is limited. The trajectories do not establish a specific additional functional group that would resolve the remaining score gap.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The fused nitrogen-heterocycle lactam/arylsulfonyl piperazine scores 0.2354681799202668; the cyclic ether/ketone relative scores 0.22956832167184824, and the methoxy biaryl N-methylpiperazine sulfonamide scores 0.22220352400833604. Carbon disulfide and the allyl azide each score 0.0, while the small hydroxylated ring acid scores 0.01347175576035981. The initial fused heterocyclic ester already reaches 0.1678386594791329. The observed gradient rewards combining several aromatic and polar structural elements over undersized fragments or a highly hydroxylated ring alone. The final seed-2 molecules spread those elements among other linkages and remain below the leading family; no unseen target structure can be reconstructed from these scores.

per_task.generated_character: The leading molecules occupy distinct compact families: an N-methyl benzamide linked to a hydroxylated, methyl-substituted fused nitrogen heterocycle; an aryl secondary alcohol connected through an amide to pyrazole; and aryl acylhydrazones bearing a pyridyl carbonyl end. The hydrazone series varies methoxy, methyl, dimethylamino and nitrile substitution while retaining aromatic rings and a carbonyl/N-N/imine connector. Conventional amides and the hydrazones look synthetically approachable by inspection, but makeability does not settle hydrazone stability or geometry. The low-score end contains highly extended polyaryl molecules, a peptide-like macrocycle, long alkyl appendages and complex polycycles. Seeds 0 and 1 reproduce the parent molecular/score sequences; seed 2 remains in the parent's aryl acylhydrazone family with changed substitutions rather than a new chemical class.
liabilities: Acylhydrazones carry possible hydrolysis, isomerization and tautomerism liabilities; the strings specify no imine geometry and supply no stability measurements.
Long-chain and highly elaborated polyaryl or peptide-like products greatly exceed the chemical size of the successful families and have extremely low visible scores.
The chemically distinct benzamide and secondary-alcohol families are not accompanied by a comparably developed set of improved analogues in their respective supplied trajectories.
missing_features: Many weak proposals fail to preserve the compact carbonyl plus nitrogen/oxygen pattern of the better examples, substituting excessive growth, different connections or strongly altered polarity.

The recurring hydrazone series lacks specified imine geometry and demonstrated stable alternative connectors at comparable size; the secondary-alcohol example lacks tetrahedral stereochemical specification. Their contribution to the score is untested.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The fused heterocycle benzamide scores 0.30950439639437716, the aryl secondary-alcohol amide 0.27475852727088185, and the dimethylamino/nitrile hydrazone 0.27374106639693657. The methoxy hydrazone scores 0.23389266666198422, whereas a final phenolic relative scores 0.07524300360256067 and a bulky sulfamate-bearing relative 0.0002262008859360815. The cited peptide-like macrocycle scores 0.0 and the long-alkyl polyaryl structure 2.103895097704417e-113. The record supports a restricted size and polar/aromatic balance, with strong sensitivity to connections and substitutions, rather than adding heteroatoms or rings indiscriminately. The digest reports a median of 0.0 at its displayed precision; this is not a count of literally zero-valued molecules. These examples do not identify a missing target-specific pharmacophore.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A phenolic bis(pyridylmethyl) benzamide scores 0.48839749189747395, while replacing its hydroxyphenyl acyl group with the cited small oxygen/nitrogen heteroaryl group gives 0.13118230142245307. In another observed series, phenolic anilinoquinazoline reaches 0.8885781306387586 while the related nitro-decorated structure gives 0.6807958477508651. Abundant rings and heteroatoms alone do not preserve the favorable chemistry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve useful functional-group connections when extending or decorating a scaffold.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support bounded changes to attachment positions, ring heteroatoms and substituents while retaining accepted favorable combinations as alternatives within each isolated scoring history. Learn which combinations matter from that history's existing scores; no fixed pharmacophore or objective identity is justified.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest maximum SMILES length is 154 in a trajectory whose final excerpt contains enormous polymethylene cyclic amidine and lactam structures, both scored 0.02885837683273086. A repeatedly amidated polyaryl molecule scores 8.44294806417311e-77, and a long-alkyl polyaryl structure scores 2.103895097704417e-113. These are real accepted structures despite their unhelpful size and connectivity.
transferable_gaps.gap: Molecular size and ring closure are not reliably controlled during scaffold elaboration.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make bounded chain extension, chemically reasonable ring closure and compact scaffold alternatives reliable capabilities. Let observed scores determine useful size regimes, without assuming every macrocycle or large molecule must be excluded.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task's stereocentre_rate is 0.0. C=C(C)c1ccccc1C(O)CNC(=O)c1cc[nH]n1 contains an asymmetric alcohol-bearing carbon but no configuration marker; C#CC(OC)c1cc2c(Nc3ccc(F)c(F)c3)ncnc2cc1F likewise leaves its substituted carbon unspecified. The repeatedly emitted aryl acylhydrazones have no specified imine geometry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The emitted structures do not specify tetrahedral stereochemistry and leave recurring imine geometry unresolved.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent and validate stereochemical alternatives when the molecular graph supports them, while preserving their connection to accepted identities. Treat any score benefit from configuration as an open question; the present labels do not establish stereoselectivity.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The top excerpts repeatedly reuse anilinoquinazoline decorations, tricyclic arylamine/diazacycle combinations, pyridyl acylhydrazones and phenolic bis(pyridylmethyl) benzamides. Other seeds contain distinct plausible amide, lactam and sulfonamide families, so the output is not globally collapsed; the limitation is sustained alternatives around the useful chemistry.
transferable_gaps.gap: Chemical diversity across the whole output is not consistently retained among its useful scaffold families.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Maintain opportunities to extend chemically distinct accepted families within the current scoring history, alongside local analogue exploration. Evaluate scaffold and attachment diversity separately from changes that only move a halogen or lengthen an alkyl tail.

transferable_gaps.evidence: COc1ccc(C=NNC(=O)c2ccncc2)cc1OC scores 0.23389266666198422 and seeds a visible substitution family, but its imine geometry is unspecified. Conventional amide families also occur among the better molecules. The record shows neither stability measurements nor a controlled comparison of equally compact alternative linkers.
transferable_gaps.gap: Stable and geometrically defined alternatives to recurrent hydrazone or imine linkages remain underdemonstrated.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Enable linkage changes that preserve approximate size and donor/acceptor placement, allowing conventional amide and other chemically credible alternatives to be tested through the same task-local labels. Do not infer stability from SMILES validity or assume a linkage replacement will improve reward.

method_name: Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy
method_thesis: Train a compact autoregressive SMILES prior solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus, then initialize a fresh policy from that prior for each objective. Use the initial observations and each subsequent scored batch to update only its highest-reward sequences with the Augmented Hill-Climb loss: fit policy log likelihood to frozen-prior log likelihood plus scaled observed reward. Sample complete molecules token by token from the updated policy, canonicalize them, and refill invalid or duplicate proposals by further generation. The corpus supplies language training, never a ranked molecular pool. Elite-conditioned policy updates should shift generation toward new high-scoring molecular combinations quickly enough to improve the benchmark's mean final Top-1. This is a small-budget transfer hypothesis, not a claim that published larger-budget gains carry over. The root uses the current scored batch; randomized historical replay is reserved for the first improvement. The anchor's elite augmented-likelihood mechanism is described by [Thomas et al.](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13321-022-00646-z).
